question.text: 'Saraswati Growth Fund' recovers INR 40 crore from an early exit within the investment period. The PPM has an explicit 'recycling' clause. What does this mean for the LPs?

answer.text: The fund must distribute the INR 40 crore immediately - no re-deployment permitted.
SEBI requires the INR 40 crore to be parked in G-Secs until fund winding up.
The manager may re-deploy the INR 40 crore into new investments, effectively reusing capital within the investment period as per PPM conditions.
LPs automatically receive a waiver on future drawdowns equal to INR 40 crore.

explanation.text: The Logic: A 'recycling' (or 're-investment') clause in the PPM allows the manager to re-deploy capital returned from an early exit into new investments within the investment period, subject to the cap and conditions in the PPM. Without such a clause, returned capital must be distributed to LPs. The Trap: 'Distribute immediately' is the default WITHOUT recycling. G-Sec parking and drawdown-waiver are fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C treats recycling as a manager-right bounded by PPM. XIX-A tests whether the distributor disclosed recycling to the LP. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating recycling caps with LPs, tie the cap to a percentage of commitments (e.g., 125%) so LPs can see the maximum potential exposure - opaque clauses cause LP disputes.
